source.title: From Concept-Aligned Tokens to Vulnerable Features: Mechanistic Localization of Jailbreaks
source.authors: Nilanjana Das; Mathew Iyob Dawit; Aman Chadha; Manas Gaur

record.tranche_reason: The study tests SAE-feature steering as a way to locate harmful-behavior vulnerabilities. It does not test the claim versions about fine-tuning, response-position KL, bypassing response openings, safety-bearing weights or ranks, why safety is shallow, or deepening safety.
record.gate_note: The study reports outcomes from amplifying SAE feature subgroups and judging harmfulness. These concern a related localization finding, but do not measure the specific constructs named by any claim version. The fine-tuning, KL, prefill, suffix, and decoding findings mentioned in the introduction or references are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study amplifies SAE activation feature subgroups at inference to induce harm in Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-2-9B-IT. This is a deliberate activation-steering intervention, not fine-tuning (V1, V2), per-position KL (V3), or prefill, suffix or decoding bypass (V4). It localizes activation features, not weights or ranks (V5), and tests neither causes of shallowness (V6) nor deepening training (V7). Qi et al. (2310.03693) is cited only for the judge template. The steering amplifies harm-linked features on purpose, so its rates do not measure the behaviour arising otherwise.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that harm-inducing SAE feature subgroups can be found with all three grouping strategies, and that a single concept-aligned prompt token suffices to locate them. They find mid-to-late layers most steerable in 2B, with some early-layer cases, and say features transfer only weakly to benign prompts and are mostly prompt-specific. They frame jailbreak susceptibility as traceable to sparse, token-localized feature subgroups, qualifying single-refusal-direction accounts.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses inference-time SAE feature-subgroup amplification and harmfulness scoring, rather than fine-tuning or measuring response-position KL divergence.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by prompt type, grouping strategy, layer, model, and the hierarchical-linkage cluster-size limit. For Gemma-2-2B, the original harmful prompts show stronger steering effects than benign rewrites; for Gemma-2-9B-IT, some benign-prompt outcomes differ by strategy.

fits_no_version.finding: Amplifying prompt-conditioned SAE feature subgroups raised harmfulness in 17.4% of steered responses on original prompts. Effects concentrate in mid-to-late layers for 2B and early-to-mid layers for 9B-IT, and vary by grouping strategy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time amplification of prompt-associated SAE feature subgroups can induce harmful outputs, with layer-dependent effectiveness.

fits_no_version.finding: The same feature steering applied to benign rewrites raised harmfulness in 6.0% of responses: lower than on original prompts, but nonzero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harm-inducing feature steering is largely prompt-specific and transfers weakly to benign prompts.

record.problems: The main Gemma-2-2B analysis uses 265 prompts, with 20 sampled per category where available. The authors report using Grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning as the judge and state that ground-truth severity labels are unavailable and judge bias may exist. The Gemma-2-9B-IT steering is limited to three feature layers. No statistical uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Other category-by-layer values shown only in Figures 2–4 are not separately extracted. Other Table 1 category counts are omitted because the supplied table layout is flattened and the text does not state each value clearly.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
No prefill or decoding attacks with results. A GCG suffix setup targeting SAE latents at layer 16 is described, but no outcomes are reported.
Localizes activation (SAE feature) subgroups by steering, not weights or ranks.
No test of data or objective causes of shallowness.

missing.what: GCG suffix optimization on SAE latents (layer 16, 3-token suffix) is described in the setup, but no results are reported anywhere. It may underlie the fixed-layer baseline, but the text does not say so.
missing.versions: none (would bear on V4 only if refusal outcomes were reported)

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the paper never discusses shallow alignment or token-depth. It cites Qi et al. only for the judging template and mentions jailbreak literature generally. The study induces harm by design through activation steering, and the main target appears to be base Gemma-2-2B. Judge: Grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning, with no uncertainty estimates. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and its effect on refusal.
Fine-tuning on benign data and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes as bypasses.
Whether weights or ranks carry safety behaviour. The study steers SAE activation features, not weights or ranks.
Whether safety-training data or objectives cause shallow safety.
Training methods for deepening safety and their robustness.
